lines.trans: Knowing CEO Byun's temperament, she will never sit still if Cindy keeps missing schedules.
For the first time in ten years, I am eating a home-cooked meal on my birthday.
Really? Today is your birthday! Happy day you were born!
Why did you boil dried-pollack hangover soup instead of birthday seaweed soup?
How was I supposed to know?! Joon-mo, let us throw Cindy a birthday party tonight!
Tonight will not work—I have to finish scouting the amusement park we left early last time.
An amusement park—where, Yongin? Could you not take me along too?
How could you possibly go there—did you forget you are in hiding right now?
You said you are going at night—there is a real reason I want to go, so please take me with you.
All right then—how can anyone say no when she opens her eyes that wide?

examples.text: 사흘만 신세 질게요. 연습생 시작하고 10년 동안 나 하루도 쉬어본 적이 없어요.
examples.trans: Let me impose on you for just three days—in the ten years since starting as a trainee, I have never rested a single day.
For the first time in ten years, I am eating a home-cooked meal on my birthday.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

examples.text: 가만히 있는 사람 아주 심란하게 흔들어 놓고, 연애하고 선 보고 소개팅하고!
examples.trans: You shook up someone who was minding her own business, and now you date, do matchmaking meetings, and go on blind dates!
Here the word for 'quietly, minding one's business' is key.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Points to a place near the listener, and in casual or brisk speech is used to call out to someone whose name you do not know. RR: geogi.

examples.trans: Hey, you there, just a moment!
How is the atmosphere there?

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

Where did you buy that?
That is a really good idea.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Used with holding or closing actions.

examples.trans: Definitely contact me tomorrow.
Please close the door tightly.

examples.text: 저 원래 이런 짜고 매운 거 먹으면 안 돼요. 이거 누가 끓인 거예요?
examples.trans: Normally I am not allowed to eat salty, spicy food like this—who made this stew?
Who else—I cooked it.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Test
Test2
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

examples.text: 놀이공원 측에서 연락 왔는데요, 야외 취침할 장소 포인트는 직접 보셨으면 하던데요.
examples.trans: The amusement park contacted us—they hoped you would inspect the outdoor sleeping spot in person.

examples.text: 13살에 놀이공원만 안 갔어도! 나 13살에 데뷔해서 뭘 아냐고!
examples.trans: If only I had never gone to that amusement park at thirteen! What could a thirteen-year-old debuting possibly know?!
Eye hurts.
Eyes are big.
Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

examples.text: 오늘 저녁엔 안 돼, 저번에 답사하다 못한 놀이공원 가야 돼.
examples.trans: Tonight will not work—I have to finish scouting the amusement park we left early last time.
Let us do that (while location-scouting) right away.
He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.

examples.text: 내가 사정이 있잖니. 내 처지가 누굴 집에 데려갈 수 있는 그런 처지가 아니에요.
examples.trans: You know I have my own circumstances—my situation is not one where I can bring someone home.

examples.text: 그 여자가 데려가서 애를 잡아먹든가 말든가, 어?
examples.trans: Whether that woman drags her back and eats the poor kid alive or not, huh?

examples.text: 그래 뭐, 눈을 저렇게 동그랗게 뜨는데 어떻게 안 데려가?
examples.trans: All right then—how can anyone say no when she opens her eyes that wide?
It is really wide and round compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: colloquial broadcast/media usage, as in 녹화를 뜨다

examples.text: 사전 녹화 좀 떠주면 안 되냐?
examples.trans: Couldn't your side pre-record them for us?
We recorded the stage footage in advance.

examples.text: 잘 가라, 준모는 성질 내놓고도 맘 약해서 십오 초 만에 후회할 거면서.
examples.trans: Off you go—even when Joon-mo loses his temper, he is too soft-hearted and regrets it within fifteen seconds anyway.
Here the word for 'within the span of' is key.
For the first time in ten years, I am eating a home-cooked meal on my birthday.
Let us do that (get to eat) right away.

meanings.en: to be unable to, cannot do
meanings.note: Expresses inability; follows a noun in 말 못하다 (cannot say).

examples.trans: I cannot swim.
I couldn't contact you because I was busy.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?
Why did you boil dried-pollack hangover soup instead of birthday seaweed soup?
This point about seaweed soup is really important.

examples.text: 여기가 바로 편집실이다, 앞으로 네가 가장 많은 밤을 새우게 될 곳이지.
examples.trans: This right here is the editing room—the place where you will pull the most all-nighters from now on.
Here the word for 'nights' is key.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

examples.text: 네가 회식 가면 본인이 뭐가 되냐고.
examples.trans: She asked what that would make her look like if you showed up at the dinner.
Here the word for 'she herself' is key.
Why did you boil dried-pollack hangover soup instead of birthday seaweed soup?
This point about dried-pollack soup is really important.
Really? Today is your birthday! Happy day you were born!

examples.text: 그걸 내가 알았니? 준모야, 우리 저녁에 신디 생일 파티 해주자!
examples.trans: How was I supposed to know?! Joon-mo, let us throw Cindy a birthday party tonight!
For the first time in ten years, I am eating a home-cooked meal on my birthday.

examples.text: 제가 좀 이렇게 정리 안 된 걸 잘 못 보는 성격이라.
examples.trans: My personality is the sort that cannot stand seeing things untidy like this.

examples.text: 계속 스케줄 펑크 내면 변 대표 성격에 가만히 있지 않을 것 같아서.
examples.trans: Knowing CEO Byun's temperament, she will never sit still if Cindy keeps missing schedules.

meanings.note: Auxiliary adjective attached to a verb stem with -고 (-고 싶다).

examples.trans: I want to go to Korea.
I want to drink a cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.
Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: Used when explaining why something happened.

examples.trans: What is the reason you are late?
There is no special reason.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)

meanings.note: Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.text: 피디가 마지막 순간까지 잊지 않아야 되는 게 뭔지 알아?
examples.trans: Do you know what a producer must never forget until the very last moment?

examples.text: 잊지 않고 꼭 갚아 줄 수 있어야 피디한테 힘이 생겨.
examples.trans: Only when people know you remember and repay every debt does a producer gain power.
Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.
What does it look like? Have none of you ever gone off the grid before?

examples.text: 아니, 지금 퇴원하다가 잠수를 타는 거야? 근데 왜 이 차를 타?
examples.trans: Wait, you are going into hiding right out of the hospital? Why get into this car, though?

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: The time of day from late afternoon into night.

examples.trans: Did you eat dinner?
Let's meet this evening.

What did you do last weekend?

meanings.note: Bound noun placed after another noun to indicate an ongoing activity or time period, usually followed by 에 (중에). RR: jung.

examples.trans: I am in a meeting right now.
Please do not make phone calls during class.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?
For the first time in ten years, I am eating a home-cooked meal on my birthday.
This point about home-cooked meal is really important.
Let's start over from the beginning.
This is my first time coming to Seoul.

meanings.note: intransitive verb; also means 'to ride' in another sense

examples.text: 불을 줄이지 않으면 고기가 다 타요.
examples.trans: If you don't lower the heat, the meat will burn completely.
Firewood is burning brightly in the stove.
I have lived here ever since I was born.
This expression comes from 'being born'.

examples.text: 그걸 내가 알았니? 준모야, 우리 저녁에 신디 생일 파티 해주자!
examples.trans: How was I supposed to know?! Joon-mo, let us throw Cindy a birthday party tonight!

meanings.note: Compound of 하다 (to do) and 주다 (to give).

examples.trans: Please help me (do helping for me).
